content: The selection of glucose-lowering medications for individuals with chronic kidney disease (CKD) has been extensively studied in key clinical trials endorsed by the American Diabetes Association (ADA). Notable trials include EMPA-REG OUTCOME, CANVAS, LEADER, and SUSTAIN-6. These studies have demonstrated the significant benefits of medications such as empagliflozin and liraglutide in mitigating the progression of CKD and reducing cardiovascular events. For instance, empagliflozin has been shown to lower the risk of end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) and slow the progression of albuminuria. Similarly, liraglutide has been found to reduce the incidence of cardiovascular events while also decelerating the progression of kidney disease. These findings emphasize the critical importance of selecting glucose-lowering therapies that not only manage blood sugar levels but also provide broader protective effects for both kidney function and cardiovascular health in patients with CKD and diabetes.
